As per office report, notice has been served on respondent no. 2 yet no one appeared on his/her behalf.
Heard learned counsel for appellant, learned A.G.A. for the State-Respondent and perused the paper book.

This Criminal Appeal under Section 14-A(2) Scheduled Castes & Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been filed questioning the correctness of the order dated 26.8.2022 passed by Additional District and Sessions Judge/Special Judge (SC/ST Act) Siddharth Nagar in Bail Application no. 1166 of 2022 arising out of Case Crime no. 101 of 2022, under Section 376, 120B IPC and Section 3(2)(V) of SC/ST Act, P.S. Chilhiya, District Siddharth Nagar whereby his prayer for bail has been rejected.

sentences.text: six months before; he developed love affairs with her and established physical relation, of which information, she given to him and her mother; thereafter he visited to the place of accused and offered him to marry his daughter; father of the appellant came and assured to marry but subsequently parents of the accused refused to marry their son with the victim.

It is contended by counsel for the appellant that prosecutrix, in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., has stated that she developed love affairs with the accused during course of treatment of her teeth and they had also established physical relations; he also took her in Siddheshwari temple where he solemnized marriage with her but subsequently, parents refused to get married and co-accused Manoj insulted her by using caste specific work as she belongs to schedule caste; victim made similar statement in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. and stated that she was having photos and videos in support of her version; accused had established physical relation with her for number of times on pretext to marry.

He next submitted that love affairs between them and physical relations are admitted but accused could not marry the victim due to the fact that she had already lodged an FIR against one Surya Pratap Bharti vide Crime no. 298 of 2021 at P.S. Shohratgarh, District Siddharth Nagar, under sections 376, 506, 504 IPC with allegation that she was acquainted with said accused from 25.2.2019; he developed love affairs and established physical relation with her by administering some intoxicating substance in the cold drink and captured her obscene photos and videos and thereafter established relations on several times by making her blackmail; she offered him to marry in the court but he did not concede; charge-sheet has been filed by the police in that case also against the named accused Surya Pratap, however, he was enlarged on bail by the co-ordinate bench of this Court vide order dated 11.7.2022.

Lastly, it is submitted that the appellant is in jail since 21.7.2022 and there is no possibility of him after being released on bail, to tamper with evidences or influence to the witnesses; accused is a doctor by profession; this is a case of consensual relationship between the prosecutrix and the accused, which is transpired from the FIR version as well as statement of the prosecutrix herself.

Learned counsel placed reliance on judgement of Hon'ble Apex Court in Sonu @ Subhash Kumar vs. State of U.P. and another reported in 2021 9 Supreme (SC) 182 wherein Hon'ble Apex Court observed that "there is no allegation to the effect that the promise to marry given to the second respondent was false at the inception.

entities.text: Sonu @ Subhash Kumar vs. State of U.P. and another reported in 2021 9 Supreme (SC) 182
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the contrary, it would appear from the contents of the FIR that there was a subsequent refusal on the part of the appellant to marry the second respondent which gave rise to the registration of the FIR.

On these facts, we are of the view that the High Court was in error in declining to entertain the petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. on the basis that it was only the evidence at trial which would lead to a determination as to whether an offence was established."

In above case also, FIR was lodged against the accused under Section 376 IPC wherein parties were in relation for about one and half years, subsequently, appellant had expressed disinclination to marry second respondent, which lead to registration of FIR.
Per contra learned AGA has vehemently opposed the prayer for bail and supported the impugned order.

He submitted that accused had developed love affairs and thereafter established physical relation with the victim, who was patient under his guidance; victim and her parents supported the FIR version and statement under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., victim also supported FIR version in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
thus the appellant does not deserve to be enlarged on bail.

sentences.text: Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, nature of offence, consensual relation admitted by the prosecutrix in her statement; victim was major at the time of incident and keeping in view the fact that the trial of the case is not likely to be concluded in near future, the appeal has substance and it is, accordingly, allowed.
Impugned order dated 26.8.2022 is, hereby, set aside.

Let appellant, Saurabh Vishwas, be released on bail in aforesaid Case Crime on his furnishing a personal bond and two reliable sureties of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(i). The appellant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence, if the witnesses are present in Court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law;

(ii). The appellant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed,
either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code;
(iii).

In case, the appellant misuses the liberty of bail and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The appellant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court default of this condition is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of his bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
